name: Unified BUS multi-task benchmark
description: Breast cancer continues to be a major global health concern for women, necessitating early and effective detection using safe and cost-effective imaging techniques like Ultrasound. The scarcity of homogenous and annotated breast ultrasound (BUS) datasets often limits automated detection using deep learning (DL) techniques. This study aims to conduct a thorough comparative evaluation of DL models for dual tasks of classification and lesion segmentation. A unified dataset was compiled using eight publicly available BUS datasets, underwent comprehensive preprocessing, and an on-the-fly data augmentation. A comparative benchmark was performed on three CNN-based architectures (EfficientNet, ResNet, DenseNet) for classification, and on U-Net variants (EfficientNet and ResNet backbones) and DeepLabV3+ for segmentation. EfficientNet-B5 reported the highest overall performance for the classification, revealing an accuracy of 0.86 and an F1-score of 0.87. For the segmentation, U-Net with EfficientNet-B7 backbone showed promising results, achieving a Dice score of 94.01% and an IoU of 90.35%. The performance of EfficientNet and U-Net architectures corroborates their potential for a robust breast cancer detection, balancing high accuracy and computational efficiency. Therefore, warranting a possibility for an optimal clinical translation of AI-assisted breast cancer diagnosis.
reputation: A domain-specific benchmark combining eight public BUS datasets that is used in breast ultrasound imaging research but is not widely adopted outside that community.
notes: Merged from multiple public BUS datasets — potential for label heterogeneity and domain shift; dataset size and diversity may be limited. Not an LLM benchmark (medical imaging).
